sections.title: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The city kills more IOS deals than the market does. Ron Rohde, reviewing a 5.5-acre graveled truck-parking site 24 months after closing, names the city the number one issue: zoning, setbacks, fire lanes, sprinklers, sewer and utility questions, with the fix being confirmation that the jurisdiction is friendly before going under contract [gcg4K6xqYaU @ 00:05:42]. The site drew 50 to 75-plus tours, including national and credit groups, and still could not sign a lease without the city's green light. Ron's next steps there are regulatory work and landing a compatible use. Benji Miller avoids that trap by front-loading the work, running heavy diligence before contract on the Fontana deal, including land-use attorney Alan Mackins, because of zoning landmines [7qT_5Pw0cTo @ 00:08:56]. Chris Long of Longyards paid for the same lesson in a different currency: 12 easements on one site caused a 2-year loss and raised costs by a third [RPNJmiZNQdY @ 00:39:23]. Chris also flags that some Texas cities limit unbuilt sites to 5 years and that in DFW a structure was required for full occupancy; the DFW location fell through, and Tier 1 land with existing heavy-industrial use is where Longyards now concentrates [7n_O1KWl4EQ @ 00:04:15].

Thin NOI plus the wrong debt is the second killer. On that same site, rents climbed from $100 per stall to $215 to $225 against a pro forma of $150, yet insurance rose several thousand dollars and net income stayed flat [gcg4K6xqYaU @ 00:04:45]. A 5-year fixed note at about 5.5% saved their bacon; Ron says variable debt plus a thin NOI would have meant pain, and calls the lender a very powerful ally but a heavy sword. Benji Miller flags the same exposure at portfolio scale: 2022 and 2023 vintage portfolios on 3-year loans face liquidity events, so expect recaps and new debt facilities [7qT_5Pw0cTo @ 00:35:08]. Evan Shelley of Truck Parking Club says a lot of underwriting in the last couple of years just made no sense, and that the lots that failed were too far out or over-leased; buying property in the middle of Kentucky or Tennessee, not close to anything, on the assumption you will fill it is not a wise decision [Ombo8TjihMk @ 00:29:46]. Expense lines are stickier than first-timers expect: AT&T's commercial minimum is $250 a month and an electric hookup alone runs $100 a month, because, as Ron puts it, you can't do anything cheaply in commercial [q7HQGiIiT_8 @ 00:29:31].

The daily grind leaks money through access, collections and tenants who abuse the yard. Rig Hut's founders, who managed a multi-yard portfolio around a South Florida port city, warn that your gate code is not a gate: codes get shared with cousins, dispatchers and buddies until you think 40 trucks are paying while 50 are parked and 3 haven't paid in 2 months, and the fix is tying access control to payment [ulBXkeE5I_8 @ 00:01:59]. One Rig Hut operator came off Zelle, Venmo, checks, cash and a single sheet of printer paper; now drivers open the gate from their phones and past-due tenants get locked out on the 10th, which generates calls [hjC6tiI5Kd4 @ 00:00:48]. Chris Long's early equity-for-management deal failed and the managers were fired; Chris now insists on a strong lease, because abandoned cars can take 3 to 6 months to remove, and on separation of duties so people can't get crooked [RPNJmiZNQdY @ 00:42:02]. Ron Rohde had a tenant swap clean fill for debris, brought in Terracon, and now watches for truck oil changes with boots on the ground, cameras and a check of all four corners [q7HQGiIiT_8 @ 00:12:03]. Tyler Cauble's add-on: always get a Phase I, even in cash deals.

chapters.question_prompt: How do cell site hardware and battery storage sites actually work, and what makes a parcel qualify for a BESS lease?
chapters.title: Under the Lease: Cell Site Technology and Battery Storage Sites
chapters.subtitle: Antennas and 5G MIMO, how a call travels through a tower, Starlink micro cell towers, BESS components (PCS, EMS, BMS), land requirements for battery storage, free land screening tools, project selection, and BESS financial modeling
chapters.executive_summary: Practitioners agree a battery storage lease is a grid-proximity play: LandGate wants 2 to 15 acres next to a substation or under half a mile away, Land Owl screens for 5 to 20 acres, power next door, a flat pad and access, and Gore Street Capital weighs land, planning, grid cost and lease length before buying ready-to-build projects. Leases run 20 to 30 years with upgrade rights. Street tools are cheap: Doxy's free site check allows 10 screenings a day and a $9.99 map, while Land Owl's map work exposes a listing asking 7.7 times its 2020 sale price. Modelers plan for 1.5 to 3.5% annual battery fade and a 20% reserve. On the tower side, SpaceX's reported push for 80,000 cell sites collides with a BNP Paribas $100 billion build estimate and critics dismissing rooftop microcells.

sections.heading: Section 1: The Practitioner Consensus
paragraphs: Every land-side operator lands on the same first filter: the wire, not the dirt. LandGate's LandApp team tells owners battery storage needs only 2 to 15 acres, a fraction of a solar farm, and that the pad should sit next to a substation or less than half a mile away [Yes7DTfUfJs @ 00:00:17]. Mickey at Land Owl runs a tighter rubric of four boxes, the right size at about 5 to 20 acres, power next door, a flat pad, and access, then measures a Yadkin County, North Carolina listing at 0.35 and 0.47 miles from an in-service Duke Energy substation carrying four 100 kV lines [yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:00:19]. Gore Street Capital's investment team scores the same variables from the buyer's chair: the cost of the grid connection, the distance to substation, the length of the land lease, and the availability of land to expand in the future all feed its investment decision [9jXkiEU8op0 @ 00:01:06]. The Power Hub goes further for UK farm and industrial owners, pitching that land with a substation already installed within it can host a self-contained battery system built in close proximity, and that the owner is handsomely rewarded for facilitating it [zXV1Vy_XECY @ 00:05:15]. Acreage is the easy part; proximity is the asset everyone is pricing.

Every engineer who walks a battery site describes the same hardware on the pad. BESS Engineer frames the business as flattening the duck curve, charging in the midday belly when solar floods the grid and discharging up the neck into the evening peak, then traces the power path from battery containers storing DC, to a skid with an inverter and transformer, to combiner switchgear, a main step-up transformer, a high-voltage switchyard, and the gantry where the utility meters every megawatt in and out [Pd5iB85hCLU @ 00:01:37]. Circuit Masterclass lists the same stack of storage battery, PCS, EMS, transformer, BMS, fire protection, and cooling, and notes lithium-ion only performs efficiently between 20 and 40 degrees C [YhDIp_Bjk-I @ 00:05:05]. IndiGrid puts dimensions on it: each container is about 20 ft long, 8 ft wide, 9.5 ft high, and weighs 43 tons [x9hN7fa_OOI @ 00:08:07], and 84 battery units across a 10-acre area form one power asset that can supply the entire evening peak of a mid-sized Indian city [x9hN7fa_OOI @ 00:23:08]. BESS Engineer's scaling rule matters for anyone holding ground under one of these plants: to make the plant bigger, you do not build a bigger machine, you repeat the station.

On paper, LandGate says battery storage leases run 20 to 30 years, the developer begins building once the lease is signed, the owner keeps access to the rest of the property because the footprint is small, and the contract has to allow periodic facility upgrades as technology changes [Yes7DTfUfJs @ 00:01:44]. Under a tower lease, the operators agree on an equally standard build. Telecom Training explains that instead of one antenna covering 360 degrees, the tower divides coverage into three sectors of 120 degrees each, which lets millions of phones share the network efficiently [tqz39K230_w @ 00:01:27]. Buildrightacademy walks the compound from the dirt up: a buried ring of bare copper with ground rods often 8 feet long and a common target of 5 ohms or less, then a walk-in shelter or slab of outdoor cabinets holding rectifiers that turn utility AC into 48-volt DC, a battery rack that carries the site for hours rather than days, the BBU, and on many sites a generator started by a transfer switch [kHmq6jr22Ms @ 00:03:06]. The same instructor says small cells, boxes about the size of a backpack hung on street poles or buildings close to the street and covering a block or two, are now nearly 40% of all US cell sites [kHmq6jr22Ms @ 00:15:04].

sections.heading: Section 2: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: Screening starts on a screen, not in a truck. Land Intel walks through sitedata.doxy.com, which tracks active 20-acre listings pre-screened for power substation and fiber proximity, then runs its free renewable energy site check under the I am a landowner investor tab, which allows 10 free screenings and two free submissions per day [P_Nhj8ZzbYw @ 00:00:54]. The operator enters acreage, in this case a 69-acre property bought after running this exact check, drops coordinates, an address, or a pin, and gets ratings for power line, substation, and fiber proximity; the $9.99 interactive map then layers parcel boundaries, FEMA flood zones, nearest substations, transmission line paths, and fiber lines [P_Nhj8ZzbYw @ 00:02:28]. Land Owl does the same work inside Land id by switching on energy, then electric, then substations and transmission lines, clicking the substation to confirm it is in service, and reading line voltages and utility ownership straight off the map [yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:01:00]. LandGate adds a battery storage value index score inside its property report and a free marketplace where owners list for sale or lease across solar, wind, oil and gas, mining, and EV charging with their contact details attached, so developers call directly with no middleman [Yes7DTfUfJs @ 00:01:27].

Mickey's Yadkin County teardown is the cleanest worked example of parcel math. The listing is just shy of 13 acres for $350,000, split across a 3.86-acre parcel and a 9.12-acre parcel, so only the combination clears the 5-acre bar [yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:00:19]. Contours turn up 11 lines from 975 to 1,025 feet, a 50-foot fall, and the soil survey shows over 95% Clifford sandy clay loam at 6 to 10% slopes; Mickey's call is that slope is a cost, not necessarily a no, so the operator prices grading, cut, fill, and maybe a retaining wall for the flat battery pad [yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:01:46]. Then the money: the smaller parcel last sold for $17,500 in July 2020 and now asks $135,450, about 7.7 times, and the pair last sold for just short of $70,000 combined against the $350,000 ask, about five times, while the listing claims TZ zoning and the map shows R20 residential and M1 industrial [yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:02:33]. The Power Hub runs the operator-side math for UK businesses: a five-day week leaves potentially 29% of weekly usage going to waste, and buying power back costs very likely 5 to 10 times what it sold for [zXV1Vy_XECY @ 00:04:18].

Revenue modeling is where a developer decides what a site is worth. eFinancial Models builds price arbitrage directly into its Excel template: charge when the grid price is low, including midday hours when solar oversupply drives prices down and sometimes negative, discharge when the evening price is high, and set battery availability at 95% of days with 5% offline [8xq5_kt3OY0 @ 00:14:31]. The same template keeps a 20% minimum load that is never discharged because battery suppliers recommend it to prolong lifetime, models annual capacity fade of 1.5 to 3.5%, and warns that running two cycles per day adds wear that forces a recheck of expected lifetime cycles [8xq5_kt3OY0 @ 00:18:30]. IndiGrid confirms that two-cycle regime at utility scale, describing India's choice of drawing 2-hour worth of energy two times a day as rare worldwide, lowering total cost of ownership while stretching the chemistry to its maximum physical limits [x9hN7fa_OOI @ 00:21:02]. Policy can rewrite the math: Learn Solar & BESS reports Rajasthan's 2025 green open access rules require any renewable project over 5 megawatt to include battery storage of at least 5% capacity for a minimum of 2 hours, offset by 75 to 100% exemptions on transmission charges [i_OH8wyz41M @ 00:02:20].

callout.title: What the operators do before anyone signs
callout.body: Four moves the practitioners use to protect price and position on a battery or tower site.
items: Trust the map over the listing: the listing tells you what you want to hear and the map shows you what you need to see, so confirm substation capacity with the utility and zoning with the county [Land Owl — yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:02:53].

Learn your state's renewable energy incentives before talking to a developer; few owners know them and understanding them gives a leg up during negotiations [LandApp by LandGate — Yes7DTfUfJs @ 00:00:51].

Start small and learn the curve: IndiGrid ran a 250 kWh pilot at one of its existing substations before bidding standalone utility-scale projects and grew to 2.5 GW [IndiGrid Infrastructure Trust — x9hN7fa_OOI @ 00:06:50].

Timing is the price: invest too early and you carry planning, land, and grid risk, too late and someone else captured the value; Gore Street uses in-house construction expertise to enter earlier at more attractive pricing [Gore Street Capital — 9jXkiEU8op0 @ 00:05:40].

sop_steps.action: Confirm the nearest substation is in service and inside half a mile, then call the utility.

sections.heading: Section 3: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: The land-side players do not agree on the size of the box or on who should stand between the owner and the developer. LandGate pegs battery storage sites at 2 to 15 acres and wants the parcel next to a substation or less than half a mile away [Yes7DTfUfJs @ 00:00:17]. Mickey at Land Owl runs a wider band of about 5 to 20 acres, stacks two parcels of 3.86 and 9.12 acres to clear the bar, then warns that close isn't the same as capacity and only the utility can tell you if that substation has room for you [yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:00:19]. Land Intel goes bigger again, pulling 20-acre listings pre-screened for substations and fiber and running a 69-acre purchase through the Doxel site check before buying [P_Nhj8ZzbYw @ 00:01:11]. The route to the developer splits three ways. LandGate offers a free marketplace listing with your contact information exposed, no middleman, and no obligation to accept any offer. Doxel screens the submission and introduces qualifying land to solar, BESS and data center developers. The Power Hub pitches the opposite of direct dealing: you bring the land, they bring the investors, the planning knowledge and the energy-supplier relationships, and they manage the whole process from start to finish [zXV1Vy_XECY @ 00:05:50].

On the capital side, the split is about when to step in and how hard to run the asset. Gore Street Capital's baseline is acquiring projects ready to build, with land, planning and grid connection secured, because investing too early means unnecessary planning, land and grid risk while investing too late means someone else already captured much of the value [9jXkiEU8op0 @ 00:02:33]. Yet the same desk says in-house construction and technical expertise lets it invest earlier than many other investors, at more attractive pricing, and calls that early entry the repeatable source of its outsized returns [9jXkiEU8op0 @ 00:05:28]. IndiGrid took a slower ladder: a 250 kWh pilot at one of its existing substations to learn the nuances, then standalone utility-scale bids, and now 2.5 GW scale [x9hN7fa_OOI @ 00:06:50]. Dispatch strategy splits the same way. The eFinancial Models template lets an operator charge only from excess solar, from all solar, or buy from the grid for price arbitrage; the modeler pushes arbitrage to fully utilize the battery while flagging that two cycles a day means more wear and tear [8xq5_kt3OY0 @ 00:25:21]. Switch to solar-only and the model drops to one charge-discharge cycle, leaving the morning uncovered unless the battery is very big.

Under the cell-site lease, the fight is whether the big tower keeps its rent or gets carved into rooftops. The Space Flight reports SpaceX in talks to access at least 80,000 US cell sites, with Crown Castle named and its CEO saying you can assume we're talking to all parties; Crown's stock jumped while AT&T and T-Mobile each fell nearly 8% [0P3b6pUkElk @ 00:06:48]. Musk then pitched a microcell you could put on your roof like a Starlink dish, scattered through densely populated areas instead of big cell towers all over the place [0P3b6pUkElk @ 00:09:54]. The skeptics hit back hard: femtocells usually cover only the area around a single building, New Street Research called the earlier femtocell plan not feasible, T-Mobile's outgoing CFO called it laughable, and Qualcomm's own executive said we're not doing small cells over here [0P3b6pUkElk @ 00:13:36]. Buildright Academy counters that small cells, backpack-sized boxes on street poles covering a block or two, are already nearly 40% of all US cell sites, while one tower covers miles [kHmq6jr22Ms @ 00:15:04]. Musk also said AT&T, Verizon and others will not go out of business, expecting bandwidth demand from AI and robots to be tremendous.

sections.heading: Section 4: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The first trap is the listing itself. Land Owl's Yadkin County, North Carolina test case asks 350,000 for just shy of 13 acres and advertises a Duke power substation a quarter mile away; the map puts it at 0.35 and 0.47 miles from the two parcels, in service with four lines at 100 kV, but nobody except the utility can confirm capacity [yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:01:00]. The cleared site is not flat: 11 contour lines cross the parcel from 975 to 1,025 feet, 50 feet of fall on Clifford sandy clay loam at 6 to 10% slopes, so grading, cut, fill and maybe a retaining wall go into the price [yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:01:23]. Then the price and zoning: one parcel last sold for $17,500 in July 2020 and now asks 135,450, about 7.7 times its last sale, the pair last sold for just short of 70,000 combined and now asks five times as much, and the listing claims TZ zoning while the map shows R20 residential and M1 industrial [yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:02:06]. LandGate adds the term trap: leases run 20 to 30 years and must allow periodic facility upgrades as technology changes [Yes7DTfUfJs @ 00:01:44]. The Land Owl verdict: the listing tells you what you want to hear.

Build-out is where the schedule breaks. IndiGrid's Sanand battery containers run about 20 feet long, 8 feet wide, 9.5 feet high and 43 tons each, and shock, vibration or temperature deviation can permanently damage internal cell structure; the site team warns any damage can lead to an explosion, and unloading one container took more than 3 hours just from trailer to ground [x9hN7fa_OOI @ 00:08:07]. Laying the heavy cables needs at least 15 to 20 people, and any damage to a cable means repeating the job [x9hN7fa_OOI @ 00:15:28]. Then the EMS data layer slipped, producing tense moments on site from a manager who was under the impression the gear was fully ready, just power plug and the project is complete [x9hN7fa_OOI @ 00:16:07]. Gore Street Capital lists the same bleed points in sequence: regulatory risk with tariffs imposed within a short duration, construction delays that heavily impact the investment case, and revenue streams that evolve so you may not have the same ones by the time you're operational [9jXkiEU8op0 @ 00:04:32]. The desk's counter is aligning construction programs with lawyers around likely regulatory changes and building a system capable of adapting rather than one locked to day-one revenue.

The economics check starts with fade. eFinancial Models cites battery capacity degradation of 1.5 to 3.5% per year depending on source, offers fading curves that accelerate with age, and treats a refill or recycling supplier bringing capacity back to 95% as a scenario only if such a supplier can be found [8xq5_kt3OY0 @ 00:15:13]. The same template runs 95% battery availability, holds 20% as a never-discharged minimum load per supplier guidance, and warns battery lifetimes are much shorter than the solar farm, triggering replacement capex or an opex refill line [8xq5_kt3OY0 @ 00:08:00]. The modeler's fix is calibration: if lifetime cycles climb too high under a two-cycle plan, adjust the expected lifetime until the numbers make sense. Learn Solar & BESS names staggering upfront capital, a dangerous reliance on imported lithium, no standardized integration policies, and ambiguous rules on recovering costs as compounding bottlenecks hitting developers all at once [i_OH8wyz41M @ 00:06:15]. On the tower side, the cost check is steel: a 5G panel is often heavier with more wind load, so an engineer runs a structural analysis against ANSI/TIA-222, and sometimes the answer is reinforce the pole first, before anyone climbs [kHmq6jr22Ms @ 00:15:43].

callout.title: Four checks before you sign, buy or climb
callout.body: Every item below comes from a trap practitioners hit or flagged on live land listings, battery sites and tower upgrades. Clear all four before money moves.
items: Get substation capacity from the utility, not the listing: the substation can be real and in service yet still have no room for you [Land Owl — yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:02:53].
Turn on contour lines and the soil survey before trusting 'cleared': 50 feet of fall on 6 to 10% slopes turns into grading, cut and fill costs [Land Owl — yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:01:23].
Confirm EMS data cabling and integration are on schedule, not just power gear, before setting a commissioning date [IndiGrid Infrastructure Trust — x9hN7fa_OOI @ 00:16:07].
Run a structural analysis on the tower before any heavier 5G panel goes up; sometimes the answer is reinforce the pole first [Buildrightacademy — kHmq6jr22Ms @ 00:15:43].

chapters.pull_quote: "The listing tells you what you want to hear. The map shows you what you need to see." Land Owl (yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:02:53).
action_checklist: Run the free Doxel site check with acreage and a dropped pin, using up to 10 screenings and two submissions per day, and only submit sites rating well on power line, substation and fiber proximity [Land Intel - Land Investing — P_Nhj8ZzbYw @ 00:00:54].
Map substations and transmission lines around the parcel and target 2 to 15 acres sitting next to a substation or under half a mile away [LandApp by LandGate — Yes7DTfUfJs @ 00:00:33].
Score every parcel on the four Land Owl tests: right size of about 5 to 20 acres, power next door, a flat pad, and road access with frontage [Land Owl — yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:00:19].
Compare the listing's zoning claim against the map and ask the county which zoning applies before making an offer [Land Owl — yVhfvSQwGRQ @ 00:02:33].

Before pitching investors, lock land, planning and grid connection, and document grid connection cost, substation distance, land lease length and room to expand [Gore Street Capital — 9jXkiEU8op0 @ 00:01:06].
Model the battery with 95% availability, a 20% minimum load reserve and annual fade before trusting any arbitrage return [eFinancial Models — 8xq5_kt3OY0 @ 00:14:31].
